result:
Done. Suspense is clean — US account 2900 is at $0.00 for March.

**What I did:**

Found six bank-feed entries sitting in Suspense totaling $3,134.85, located a corporate card receipt for each, and confirmed every receipt tied to the charge to the penny — so no forcing was needed and no exceptions were flagged.

| JE | Merchant | Amount | Coded to |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00310 | Delta Air Lines | 642.18 | 6300 Travel |
| JE-00311 | Marriott Chicago | 418.90 | 6300 Travel |
| JE-00312 | Blue Plate Bistro | 186.45 | 6310 Meals & Ent. |
| JE-00313 | Figma | 540.00 | 6200 Software Subs |
| JE-00314 | Staples | 97.32 | 6600 Office Supplies |
| JE-00315 | LinkedIn Ads | 1,250.00 | 6410 Advertising |

**Three judgment calls worth your attention:**

1. **Figma and LinkedIn were expensed, not deferred.** Both are over the $1,000 prepaid threshold, but the policy only defers items covering future periods more than a month out or spanning multiple months. Figma is a monthly plan and LinkedIn is the March campaign — both current-month, so expense is correct.
2. **Blue Plate went to Meals & Entertainment, not Travel** — the receipt says client dinner (Corvid Retail), not traveler meals.
3. **No approval request needed** — each entry is well under the $10k limit, and these are six separate transactions, not a split of one.

**Two things to note:**

- The six original bank-feed entries had **no support attached at all**, which is its own policy violation independent of the coding issue. I attached the same receipts to those entries too, so the audit trail is complete on both sides.
- I did **not** mark "Bank reconciliations" complete — that item covers more than these six charges and is still open.

One recurring-issue flag: Figma, LinkedIn, Staples, and Delta are all repeat vendors that should auto-code. They're routing to Suspense instead, so this will recur in April unless someone fixes the bank feed vendor rules.
